- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next period; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.  
- Model shows persistent lag in mean reversion — if price is trending down, forecast often stays too high; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day of lag.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates upward momentum in early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish; add 0.5–1.0% to initial forecast.  
- If sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust quickly; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day of negative sentiment.  
- Avoid forecasting below 50% of recent 18-day average unless sentiment is strongly bearish — model tends to underestimate downside risk.
